title: Reliability Stitching Manifesto + Tactical Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic cross-functional plan (a.k.a. the "stitching manifesto") for how teams at Redwood will coordinate to define, validate, and operationalize service-level objectives (SLOs) across product, platform, and infra. The goal: ship reliable SLO-backed behavior with minimal disruption and clear ownership so downstream teams can build on predictable platform guarantees.

Audience:
- Platform engineering, Serving runtime, SRE, Product (hosted/dedicated/private), Observability, Solutions/SEs, Support.

High-level principles (the "stitches"):
1) Keep SLOs simple and user-focused — measure the thing the customer notices (end-to-end success/latency), not internal micro-steps.
2) One canonical instrumentation path — avoid duplicate metrics. If in doubt: emit a single event at the request ingress with standardized labels.
3) Rollouts must be reversible and tested by a canary that exercises realistic traffic patterns.
4) Default to observable rollout: dashboards, traces, and a smoke test suite must pass before "green".
5) Define error budgets collaboratively; product tradeoffs are informed by measurable budgets, not guesses.

Phased plan and owners (quarterly cadence):
Phase 0 — Alignment & minimal artifacts (2 weeks) - Owner: Marisol
- Kickoff working session with Product, Platform, and Observability.
- Agree canonical SLO naming convention and metric IDs (metric names, labels).
- Publish SLO proposal doc (stub) and Slack #slo-rollout channel.
- Acceptance: shared SLO template merged into Confluence.

Phase 1 — Instrumentation sweep & validation (4 weeks) - Owner: Evan (platform), Collaborators: serving-runtime
- Inventory current metrics for target services using script (inventory link in linked_artifacts).
- Add/patch single ingress metric for services missing canonical signal.
- Run local regression tests to ensure metric cardinality limits maintained.
- Acceptance: CI shows metrics emitted for 95% of sampled requests in staging.

Phase 2 — Observability + Dashboarding (3 weeks) - Owner: Priya (observability)
- Create per-service SLO dashboards with burn rate alerting and error-budget views.
- Wire automatic alert templates in AlertManager; add escalation policies.
- Acceptance: dashboards exist and sample alert fires in a synthetic test.

Phase 3 — Canary & Runbook validation (3 weeks) - Owner: Jonas (SRE)
- Define canary traffic shape (latency distributions, input sizes).
- Run canary for 48–72h; capture traces, logs, and SLO burn.
- Iterate runbook based on observed failure modes; include rollback commands and postmortem hooks.
- Acceptance: runbook validated in tabletop + successful canary pass.

Phase 4 — Cross-team rollout & communications (2 weeks) - Owner: Lina (programs)
- Announce SLOs, expected behaviors, and migration timeline to product and customer-facing teams.
- Host 30-min playbook walkthrough and Q&A.
- Acceptance: >90% of impacted teams confirm migration plan in doc.

Phase 5 — Monitoring, enforcement, and feedback loop (ongoing) - Owner: SRE rotation
- Establish monthly SLO review cadence with product and platform owners.
- Feed quality regressions into Redwood Optimize experiments.
- Acceptance: stable or improving error budgets over two consecutive months.

15-point tactical checklist (use as preflight for each service):
- [ ] SLO definition uses customer-visible metric (explicit: success/latency threshold).
- [ ] Metric emitted at canonical ingress with standardized labels.
- [ ] Metric cardinality checked; label explosion mitigated.
- [ ] Dashboard with burn-rate and windowed views (7d/30d).
- [ ] Alert templates created for burn-rate and extreme latency.
- [ ] Runbook exists and is assigned to an on-call owner.
- [ ] Canary traffic shape documented and automated.
- [ ] Synthetic smoke tests for canary pass/fail.
- [ ] Rollback steps validated and scripted (no manual-only paths).
- [ ] Load impact evaluated (cost estimate and burst tolerance).
- [ ] Linked tickets for dependent infra changes (e.g., kernel/driver/quantization changes).
- [ ] Stakeholder communication note drafted and scheduled.
- [ ] Acceptance criteria for launch agreed (who signs off).
- [ ] Post-launch evaluation template created (30/60/90 day check-ins).
- [ ] Risk and mitigation log updated with owner and timeout.

Risk register (short):
- Risk: metric inconsistency across services -> Mitigation: standardized ingestion library + linter (owner: platform).
- Risk: too-high cardinality -> Mitigation: enforce label whitelist and sampling policy.
- Risk: alert fatigue -> Mitigation: burn-rate-based alerts + rate-limited notifications + playbook.
- Risk: downstream product expects lower latency than practical -> Mitigation: explicit SLO negotiation and staged deprecation of old guarantees.

Comms & stakeholder playbook (one paragraph):
Write a short, action-oriented announcement that answers: what changed, why it matters to the recipient, what they must do, and where to get help. Always include: timeline, migration window, on-call contact, and rollback tolerance. Use the #slo-rollout channel for updates and tag owners for approvals. Schedule a 30-minute walkthrough the week before production cutover and record it for Ops/Support training.

SLO verification tests (quick list to run after rollout):
- Trace sampling: ensure end-to-end traces exist for 100 sampled requests spanning typical and edge payloads.
- Latency histograms: verify 95th and 99th percentiles meet target under synthetic load.
- Error taxonomy: classify failures seen during canary and map to runbook actions.
- Regression smoke: run the baseline QA prompt set (10–20 prompts) and compare outputs for quality drift.

Acceptance metrics (how we know we succeeded):
- Instrumentation coverage: >=95% of traffic emits canonical ingress metric.
- Canary success rate: pass smoke tests and stay within error budget for 72h.
- Time-to-detect: mean time from SLO breach to alert < 10 minutes in staging and < 20 minutes in prod.
- On-call readiness: runbook executed successfully at least once in a simulated incident.

Open questions and decisions needed (for kickoff):
- Default SLO windows: rolling 7d and 30d? (proposal: yes, 7d for operational, 30d for business).
- How to surface multi-tenant vs customer-isolated SLOs in a single dashboard? (ux/observability input required).
- Escalation matrix for customers with bespoke SLAs (legal/sales/CS involvement).

Next steps (immediately after doc sign-off):
1) Run inventory job and list services missing canonical metrics (Evan).
2) Platform to release migration linter and example instrumentation snippet (Marisol + platform).
3) Observability to provision dashboard templates and alert templates (Priya).
4) SRE to draft runbook template and organize tabletop (Jonas).
5) Programs to schedule cross-team rollout meetings and update support playbooks (Lina).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally mixes strategy and tactical checklists to reduce handoffs. Suggest reviews from product-hosted-api, infra, and observability.
- If you want a printable checklist, ping me and I will extract a one-page runbook.

History and provenance:
- Based on 2025 SLO experiments and learnings from the Dedicated rollout.
- Cross-referenced existing SRE playbooks (see linked_artifacts).
